gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-amarna: Amarna draws its strokes without contrast, leaving every small counter unclogged and contemporary. And Bruno Ace sits above it as the expressive voice, its ruler-straight line giving the page a bold header with a quiet follower.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-andika: Andika holds its tails and terminals as thick as its stems, with s shapes that turn wide and easy. And Bruno Ace is the one for showy, ruler-drawn display lettering, while the body font simply gets on with being modern and approachable.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-anta: Distinctive is the first word for Bruno Ace, whose connected counters and constant-width line feel bent from wire. And it earns its keep in big, short headings, while Anta lends the text a gaping-mouthed e and a professional tone.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-ar-one-sans: AR One Sans reads modern, with brush ends lifting away before each curve closes. Bruno Ace lays its heading out like spaghetti in letters, and the two feel like a loud sign beside a soft handwritten note.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-assistant: Assistant keeps the mouths of its c, e and a open, while Bruno Ace draws a thread of ink that never swells or tapers. Pages of it would read smoothly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-asta-sans: Bruno Ace lingers over each character, its counters open to the outside and its line drawn as if by ruler. Asta Sans runs on in tubelike, constant-weight strokes, and its e never turns into a blot over a long read.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-barlow: Barlow reads approachable, with c shapes whose tips pull well apart. Bruno Ace is the neon-bright heading, so a larger size for it and a modest one for Barlow would let both do their jobs.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-biz-udgothic: Bent-paperclip headings meet a body with a wide channel into every bowl, all in Bruno Ace's expressive, never-swelling line. Bruno Ace is best at display flair, while BIZ UDGothic gets on with quiet, modern text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-biz-udpgothic: Fixed-nib strokes, one character per beat: that is Bruno Ace, distinctive and expressive up top. BIZ UDPGothic is generously spaced, with a clear channel into each round letter, so a size close to ordinary text lets it breathe.
